analisis-incidente.title: Análisis del Incidente
analisis-incidente.description: The voltage collapse of 28 April was not an instantaneous event33:29 CEST — allows precise identification of the physical mechanisms that no conventional protection automation could arrest.

analisis-informes.title: Análisis de los Informes Oficiales
analisis-informes.description: The cross-analysis of the four reports on the 28 April blackout reveals an architecture of disputes that goes well beyond technical disagreement: three institutionally opposed narratives of the same sequence of events, with direct legal, economic and regulatory implications. This chapter examines the internal coherence of each narrative, their verified points of consensus, and their irreconcilable contradictions.

conclusiones.title: Conclusiones
conclusiones.description: This chapter closes the forensic analysis by articulating two complementary planes 28 April 2025 is not a frequency incident, but a voltage collapse in the Q-V plane, and that distinction is the axis on which the entire subsequent argumentative architecture pivots.

contexto.title: Contexto Técnico
contexto.description: Generation fleet evolution: from synchronous machines to IBR-dominated mix

dimension-europea/coordinacion-continent.title: Coordinación Continental
dimension-europea/coordinacion-continent.description: The abrupt separation of the Iberian Peninsula from the Continental European synchronous system was not merely an infrastructure incident: it was the first real-conditions test of the pan-European power grid governance architecture designed following the great European blackout of 2006. This chapter documents how that institutional architecture responded — its speed, its successes and its limitations — from the first seconds of the collapse to the final resynchronisation.

dimension-europea/dia-despues.title: El Día Después: Reformas Institucionales
dimension-europea/dia-despues.description: 28 April 2025 did not close its effects with the restoration of electricity supply. It opened a period of accelerated institutional revision in which ENTSO-E, ACER and national regulators across the European Union rewrote, within eight months, a set of methodologies that had remained unchanged for years. This section documents the reforms not covered elsewhere in this work — those relating to reserve capacity architecture, resource adequacy, the PICASSO platform, the new network strength metric and national political responses — completing the picture of the incident's continental-scale consequences.

dimension-europea/francia-portugal.title: El impacto en Francia y Portugal
dimension-europea/francia-portugal.description: The 28 April Iberian voltage collapse did not stop at the Pyrenees or the Guadiana. The violence of the electrodynamic transient radiated a shockwave through the interconnections, subjecting the French network to extreme operational stress and dragging the Portuguese system into a total blackout from which it could only emerge through seventeen hours of ground-up restoration. These two episodes — one contained, one catastrophic — precisely illustrate the conditions that determine whether a system can reject a perturbation of this magnitude or succumb to it.

impacto-comunicativo.title: Impacto Comunicativo
impacto-comunicativo.description: The 28 April blackout generated a second, parallel crisis alongside the electrical one: a communicative crisis whose consequences for public understanding of the incident persist well beyond supply restoration. This chapter analyses how media and social networks processed a technically complex phenomenon, and what gap opened between the expert reports' technical consensus and the narrative that reached the Spanish public.

intro.title: Welcome
intro.description: Technical Analysis of the Iberian Blackout — April 28, 2025

introduccion.title: Introducción
introduccion.description: On 28 April 2025, the Iberian synchronous system suffered a voltage collapse that destroyed more than 15 GW of generation within seconds and left nearly 60 million people without electricity. In terms of magnitude and propagation speed, the event has no precedent in the continental European power system in recent decades. This work is not a chronological reconstruction of the blackout: it is a critical, comparative analysis of the competing technical, regulatory and operational narratives formulated in its aftermath.

reaccion-reposicion.title: Reacción y Reposición
reaccion-reposicion.description: Following the voltage zero at 1230 CEST, the peninsular power system transitioned from an uncontrollable dynamic crisis to a phase of emergency management and structural restoration. The loss of over 15 GW and total disconnection from the continental synchronous system forced REE to abandon steady-state operating logic and activate the emergency protocols of Operating Procedure P.O. 1.6. Full supply restoration required nearly 19 hours of uninterrupted manoeuvring.

referencias.title: Referencias
referencias.description: Compilation of technical sources used in the analysis of the Iberian blackout on April 28, 2025.

resiliencia-futuro.title: Resiliencia y Futuro
resiliencia-futuro.description: The structural lesson of 28 April does not reside in the collapse itself, but in the class of vulnerability it revealed. The forensic analysis demonstrated that the voltage zero was not a failure of active power reserves nor an isolated operational error: it was the terminal manifestation of a fundamental incompatibility between the physics of an inverter-dominated system and a technical-regulatory framework designed for synchronous networks. The scenario that produced the 28 April event — high IBR penetration, scarce coupled synchronous generation and depressed net demand — was not a climatic anomaly, but a preview of conditions that will recur with increasing frequency as decarbonisation advances.

uso-ia.title: Uso de Inteligencia Artificial
uso-ia.description: This thesis was developed under an atypical methodological context: the simultaneous occurrence, during 2024–2026, of a systemic crisis in the Iberian power system and an accelerated transformation in natural language processing tools. The availability of Large Language Models (LLMs) capable of processing hundreds of pages of technical documentation within minutes coincided with the publication, within a single year, of four primary expert reports and a dozen academic analyses of the same event. This chapter transparently documents how these tools were integrated, what specific tasks they performed, what systematic errors were detected and corrected, and what epistemological reflection this experience yields for engineering research practice.
